name: USS Omaha
shortDescription: Gun-and-torpedo hybrid light cruiser with real bite at close range.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: Unlimited charges, 5s action, 60s cooldown. Quicker reset than a battleship's, slower than a destroyer's.

consumables.name: Sonar
consumables.flavor: 2 charges, 90s active on a 180s cooldown. Pings ships out to 3.7 km and torpedoes at 2.7 km.

consumables.name: Catapult Fighter
consumables.flavor: 2 charges, 100s uptime on an 80s cooldown. It's her only answer to enemy planes, no on-demand Defensive AA Fire in this kit.

turrets.note: Forward twin turret. Tracks far enough forward that she keeps some main battery firepower while bow-in, unusual for a cruiser.

turrets.label: Port Fwd
turrets.note: Single-gun casemate mounts, welded to their own side of the hull. Can't cross to fire starboard.
Aft twin turret, mirrors turret 1's forward-friendly coverage from the stern.

torpedoMounts.label: Port 1
torpedoMounts.note: All four mounts are fixed to their own broadside, no centerline swing. Commit to a side before you fire.

strengths: Twelve guns split across turrets and casemates, more firepower than most cruisers see this early
Both twin turrets track far enough forward to keep shooting while bow-in, an unusual angle advantage for a cruiser
Four torpedo mounts and twelve tubes total give a big spread if you can close the gap
Sonar gives her a way to spot hidden ships and incoming torpedoes that most tier IV cruisers don't have
weaknesses: Large detection radius (11.1 km sea, 6.7 km air) makes it hard to stay hidden
Thin armor (6-76mm) is an easy citadel for battleships and cruisers alike
No self-heal. Damage Control Party only handles fire and flooding, so chip damage just piles up over a match
Torpedo tubes are fixed one per side, no centerline swing, so you're committed to a broadside before you fire
Short 5.5 km torpedo range forces a genuinely risky approach to use them
tips: Don't show your broadside near anything with big guns. You will eat a citadel.
Use islands to peek, fire, and duck back before return fire lands. There's no Repair Party to undo a mistake.
Pick your side before you commit to a torpedo run. The tubes are welded to one broadside, not centerline.
Save Sonar for when you actually need to confirm a threat, not just to run it on cooldown.

threats.reason: They outspot you and can torpedo you before you even know they're there.

threats.threat: Battleships at close to mid range
threats.reason: One well-aimed AP salvo can citadel you through that thin armor.

summary: Twelve-gun hybrid cruiser, more firepower than a tier IV cruiser has any right to.
Thin-skinned, one citadel hit from a battleship ends the fight.
Torpedoes turn any overextending enemy into a mistake, if you get the right broadside on them.
playstyle.detail: Omaha rewards a bit of aggression as long as it's controlled. Twelve guns spread across turrets and casemates put fire on a target faster than most tier IV cruisers can answer, and the torpedoes make anyone who overextends regret it. But the armor is thin and there's no Repair Party to lean on, so the whole game is choosing when to be seen. Peek, shoot, pull back, and do it again.

imageCredit: USS Omaha (CL-4) anchored in the Hudson River, 2 May 1927. Naval History and Heritage Command, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

goalTags.note: Twelve guns of HE output makes her one of the better fire-spam cruisers at her tier.
Four triple mounts, twelve tubes total. Single-torpedo damage isn't exceptional, but the volley size is.
Sonar pings hidden ships and torpedoes, a spotting tool most tier IV cruisers don't get.
